input.content: Pattern: new protocol field made mandatory in an independently shipped consumer before the provider half lands. Example: settings client sent `require_receipt: True` and raised unless `response["applied"] is True` on every save, while the receipt-producing provider task was still pending and the README required support for the released provider (tag baseline) with the feature flag off. The `enhanced_settings` flag only echoed in the return value and gated nothing. The sole unit test faked the new response shape, so it encoded the assumption instead of testing the released shape. Check for: unconditional strict checks on newly added response fields; flags that don't gate the new request/response contract; missing test using the released provider's exact response. Fix shape: additive tolerance (reject only an explicit negative receipt; treat absent receipt as legacy success when released `ok` already means applied), send new request keys only behind a capability or flag, and add a test for the legacy response.
